FGO_EVENT_FINAL_UNDERWORLD.title: The Underworld at the End
FGO_EVENT_FINAL_UNDERWORLD.pages.INITIAL:
You discover a strangely silent expanse of stars.
The stars do not move. Even time seems to have stopped.
A girl stands in the middle of a dark garden.
She looks at you, seemingly even more surprised than you are.
"...No one is supposed to come here."
After a moment of silence, she adds quietly:
"But since you're already here... would you like to stay for a while?"
FGO_EVENT_FINAL_UNDERWORLD.pages.SUGAR.d:
"Really?"
She visibly relaxes.
"That's good."
She takes out a small piece of sugar that glitters with starlight.
"It's Goddess Sugar."
"It's just an ordinary offering, so don't get the wrong idea."
FGO_EVENT_FINAL_UNDERWORLD.pages.SUGAR.o: Accompany her deeper into the Underworld.
You follow her deeper into the sea of stars.
The silent Underworld gradually grows brighter.
The girl's expression seems more relaxed than before.
"...This isn't so bad."
She speaks softly.
"The end doesn't seem quite so frightening when there's someone to walk beside you."
She turns back to you.
"So... will you keep walking with me?"
FGO_EVENT_FINAL_UNDERWORLD.pages.GIFT.de:
You have reached the deeper reaches of the Underworld.
The girl stops before a vast gate of stars.
There is no path beyond it.
Only countless stars that have already ended, and those yet to come.
She holds out her hand.
"There's one last thing."
"But this time... it isn't hospitality."
You place three Saint Quartz in her hands.
She pauses.
"...All three?"
For a moment, she says nothing.
"Thank you."
The starlight vanishes into her hands.
After a long silence, a Star Sword appears, as though buried at the very edge of the universe.
"This is for those who make it this far."
"I think... this is the right time to give it to you."
FGO_EVENT_FINAL_UNDERWORLD.pages.REFUSED:
"...I see."
She does not try to persuade you.
"Then... stay here for a while."
FGO_EVENT_FINAL_UNDERWORLD.pages.LEFT.de:
"...I see."
She lowers her gaze.
"That's fair. This is the Underworld, after all."
Her expression returns to the composed demeanor of a goddess.
"Then, this is where we part."
